ratifications.statement: Account-level Terms/Privacy acceptance is required before product access, distinct from and prior to any organization-level commercial acceptance. Organization commercial acceptance is a separate act. The accepting role for organization commercial acceptance is organization_admin. Acceptance binds the specific legal instrument, its version, a content hash, and a timestamp — not merely a boolean flag. Reacceptance is required only when a governed reaccept_required version transition occurs, not on every login or unrelated change. Registration is an atomic bootstrap: organization creation, founder membership, CommercialAccount creation, an initial entitlement/bootstrap state, and an audit record are all part of one atomic operation, not a sequence of independently-failable steps. Invitation acceptance is a mutation and must occur via POST (or another proper mutating verb), never as a side effect of a render-time GET request. The physical database-level incompatibility between a single-active-membership ceiling and multi-organization membership must be removed. Legal review of the acceptance instruments and flow remains mandatory regardless of implementation status.

clauses.text: Account Terms/Privacy acceptance required before product access.
Organization commercial acceptance is a separate, distinct act.
Accepting role for organization commercial acceptance is organization_admin.
Acceptance binds instrument identity, version, content hash, and timestamp.
Reacceptance triggers only on a governed reaccept_required version transition.
Atomic bootstrap: organization + founder membership + CommercialAccount + initial entitlement/bootstrap state + audit, as one atomic operation.
Invitation acceptance must be a POST mutation, not a render-time GET side effect.
The single-active-membership physical incompatibility with multi-org membership must be removed.
Legal review remains mandatory.

ratifications.statement: There is exactly one canonical commercial state machine governing entitlement and billing, not multiple competing ones. The first Stripe customer/subscription binding originates from the CommercialAccount, occurs before checkout, and is idempotent. No commercial identity may be first-established from a webhook payload or a checkout success_url callback. A recoverable past_due state does not immediately remove product capacity. An unpaid or canceled state closes commercial capacity. Cancellation closes both entitlement grants and the active subscription identity together. An ACTIVE_WITHOUT_STRIPE state may only be reached by explicit manual activation, never inferred. Billing/commercial event ordering must be persisted, and a stale state regression (an out-of-order or superseded event) must be rejected, not applied. Prices and discounts are not frozen by this ratification.

clauses.text: One canonical commercial state machine.
First Stripe binding originates from CommercialAccount, pre-checkout, idempotent.
No first commercial identity from webhook or success_url.
Recoverable past_due does not immediately remove product capacity.
Unpaid/canceled closes commercial capacity.
Cancellation closes entitlement grants and active subscription identity together.
ACTIVE_WITHOUT_STRIPE only via explicit manual activation.
Event ordering persisted; stale state regression rejected.
Prices/discounts not frozen by this ratification.

ratifications.statement: No general-purpose job queue is required to satisfy this ratification. A durable email_deliveries record is required. That record is written in the same transaction (row-transactionally) as the logical invitation (or other triggering) event, not as an afterthought. The provider send attempt happens after that transaction commits, never before. A resend rotates the delivery token; the raw token is not persisted for reuse on resend. The delivery record's status is one of: queued, accepted, failed_retryable, failed_permanent, cancelled. 'accepted' by the provider is explicitly distinct from 'delivered'. Automatic retry may be deferred to a future authority; a manual resend path must exist regardless. Partial erasure (erasure_partial) is retryable, not terminal. Demo/lead requests must be durably recorded. Retention of these records is governed by HPO-F.

clauses.text: No general queue required.
Durable email_deliveries record required.
Written row-transactionally with the logical invitation event.
Provider send attempt occurs after commit.
Resend rotates the token; raw token not stored for resend.
Status vocabulary: queued / accepted / failed_retryable / failed_permanent / cancelled.
'accepted' != 'delivered'.
Automatic retry may be deferred; manual resend required regardless.
erasure_partial is retryable, not terminal.
Demo/lead requests must be durably recorded.
Retention governed by HPO-F.

ratifications.statement: Platform admin has no standing (always-on, un-time-bounded) access to tenant content. AAL2/MFA is required for platform admin actions and for any destructive or high-risk operation. Tenant-content support access must be tenant-authorized, purpose-bound, time-expiring, and must not auto-renew. Destructive deletion requires a distinct two-person approval, a fresh AAL2 challenge at the time of the destructive action, an explicit reason, a typed confirmation, and an audit record. A tenant's own super_admin role is not the same principal or privilege as platform admin.

Tenant-content support access: tenant-authorized, purpose-bound, expiring, no auto-renew.

Tenant super_admin != platform admin.

ratifications.statement: The F18 release-certification gate ledger is the canonical release readiness model; it is not duplicated or replaced by a competing ledger. Before any hosted DDL is applied, a fresh observation, a backup/restore plan, a compatibility plan, the exact migration corpus, and a successor ACL (access control list) must all be in place. Browser-driven golden journeys are exercised with Playwright. CI must run against an exact SHA with collected-file reconciliation, not a loosely-scoped run. Staging schema and code must reach parity while provider capabilities remain dark, before browser/provider gates are attempted. Browser/provider gates are attempted only after that parity is reached. Release Candidate (RC) status follows only after browser/provider gates pass. Production requires recovery evidence, observability, security and legal signoff, and a normal integration-branch-to-main lineage — not a shortcut merge.

Playwright for browser golden journeys.
Exact-SHA CI + collected-file reconciliation.
Staging schema/code parity while provider capabilities dark.
Then browser/provider gates.
Then RC.
Production requires recovery evidence, observability, security/legal signoff, and normal integration->main lineage.
